problem: Existing EQA benchmarks can be solved well by blind language models that see only the question, so accuracy does not show whether a model grounds its answers in the environment. Balancing answers across the whole dataset does not remove per-question language priors.
motivation: EQA agents such as search-and-rescue robots must answer from what they perceive, not from typical world knowledge. A benchmark is needed where a blind model provably cannot beat chance, so that grounded and ungrounded models can be told apart.
key_idea: Build a per-question balanced EQA dataset in which every question is paired with two Minecraft environments that yield two different correct answers, so a model that ignores the environment is at chance.
insight: Per-question balancing removes language priors: blind GPT-4o scores 50.7% (p=0.81, chance level), while GPT-4o with oracle human screenshot sequences scores 82.7%. The vision-minus-blind gap is 32.0 points, versus 1.8 on EQA v1 and 6.3 on A-EQA, so the benchmark separates grounded from blind models. Human logs (mean 278.8 actions per question, only three recordings needing no action) show that active exploration is required, not just static VQA.
method: Environments: 312 single-biome 60x60-block Minecraft worlds built with WorldEdit (city, town, cave, desert, mansion, nether, plains, snow), compatible with MineRL 1.0.

Question collection: paid expert Minecraft player pairs played cooperative mini-games (can-you-do-it, spot-the-difference) with a questioner and an agent; questions were transcribed (Whisper plus manual correction) and taken from the dialogs.

Question curation: at least two annotators labelled each question as suitable, suitable-with-context, or unsuitable; context-dependent questions were rephrased to stand alone using the previous five turns, and the rest were discarded.

Per-question balanced answers: each question is matched to two environments with different answers, using save-file lookups for some questions and manual search for others. The two answers form a two-option multiple-choice item. Tuples were verified by human play-through, and questions with the same answer in both environments were removed.
Human play data: screenshots recorded once per second and action logs once per tick (forward, jump, left, right, camera), used as oracle observation sequences and to show that action is needed.
Evaluation protocol: blind text-only GPT-4o versus GPT-4o given oracle screenshot sequences, scored by accuracy with a two-tailed binomial test against chance.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, frozen, text-only vs with vision)
setting.observation: Minecraft first-person screenshots (one per second from human play), or none for the blind model
setting.action_space: Minecraft keyboard/mouse actions (forward, jump, left, right, camera); oracle human action sequences are used in the experiments, not agent-chosen actions
setting.privileged: Oracle human-play screenshot sequences (oracle actions) are given to the vision model.

numbers.extra: question and answer choices only; no images
oracle screenshot sequences from human play recordings
numbers.evidence: Table 1: GPT4-o with Vision Acc. 0.827, p < 0.0001

numbers_note: The benchmark has 424 tuples. There is no official split, so 'test' is used as a placeholder. Yes/No vs other question breakdown (Table 3): blind 0.509/0.505, vision 0.796/0.861.
results: Blind GPT-4o reaches 50.7% accuracy, which is not significantly different from chance (p=0.81). GPT-4o with oracle screenshots reaches 82.7% (p<0.0001), a 32-point gap compared with 1.8 (EQA v1) and 6.3 (A-EQA) on prior benchmarks. The gap holds for both yes/no and other question types.
limitations: Only GPT-4o is evaluated, and only with oracle screenshot sequences; no end-to-end agent chooses its own actions.
Multiple-choice format with two options, so it cannot evaluate answer generation; English only; non-photorealistic Minecraft; 424 tuples is too few for training.
builds_on: Per-question balancing from VQA (Goyal et al. 2017; Zhang et al. 2016)
compares_to: EQA v1 (Ilinykh et al. 2022 blind analysis)
